questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A company with three departments (Marketing, Finance, Engineering) is moving to Google Cloud. Each department has development and production environments with several projects each. Department leads must administer all projects in their department, and a central security team must apply controls across all production projects. How should the engineer structure the resource hierarchy?
options: Use one project per department and separate the environments with labels.
Use department folders holding `dev` and `prod` subfolders, with leads granted on their folder.
Use a separate organization for each of the three departments.
Put all projects directly under the organization, with IAM granted on each project.
questions.correct_rationale: Folders group projects so IAM and organization policies can be applied once and inherited by everything beneath, matching departmental administration and environment separation.
questions.distractor_summary: Labels don't enforce access boundaries, multiple organizations fragment central governance, and per-project grants don't scale.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A contractor was granted the Viewer role at the organization level for an audit. The audit is over for the `payroll` project, so an administrator removed the contractor's Viewer role binding from `payroll`, but the contractor can still view resources there. Other projects must remain visible. What should the administrator do?
options: Remove and re-add the contractor's account in Cloud Identity to reset the access for the application.
Grant the contractor a custom role that has no permissions on the `payroll` project for the application.
Move the `payroll` project to a different organization to separate it from the audit in every region.
Create an IAM deny policy on `payroll` for the contractor, since inherited allows can't be removed.
questions.correct_rationale: IAM allow policies are inherited and additive, so a role granted at the organization applies to every project and can't be revoked lower in the hierarchy; deny policies can block specific permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Adding an empty custom role grants nothing and doesn't subtract, recreating the account doesn't change the org-level binding, and moving organizations is disproportionate.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A company manages 4,000 employees in on-premises Microsoft Active Directory. It wants users and groups automatically provisioned in Cloud Identity, and employees to sign in to Google Cloud with their existing corporate passwords without Google storing them. What should the engineer implement?
options: Use Google Cloud Directory Sync for users and groups, with SAML single sign-on via the identity provider.
Create the users by hand in the Admin console and require new passwords from them.
Create a service account for every one of the employees of the company.
Use Cloud Directory Sync with password synchronization and no single sign-on.
questions.correct_rationale: GCDS automates one-way provisioning of users and groups from Active Directory, and SAML SSO delegates authentication to the corporate IdP so passwords stay on-premises.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual creation doesn't scale, service accounts are for workloads rather than people, and password sync stores password hashes in Google, which the company wants to avoid.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A startup wants its 25 engineers to use Google Cloud with company-managed identities under its domain. It doesn't use or want to pay for Gmail, Docs, or other Google Workspace apps. What should the engineer set up?
options: Use personal Gmail accounts that are added to IAM for the engineers across the subscriptions.
Use a Google Workspace Business Starter subscription for the engineers across the subscriptions.
Use Cloud Identity Free, verifying the domain to get the organization and managed accounts.
Use service accounts with downloaded keys for each of the engineers.
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Identity Free provides managed identities and an organization resource without Workspace apps or cost.
questions.distractor_summary: Personal Gmail accounts aren't centrally managed, Workspace adds unwanted cost, and service account keys for humans are a security risk.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: An operations team of 30 engineers changes often as people join and leave. Each engineer needs the same set of four predefined roles in five projects. Administrators spend hours updating IAM bindings. What should the engineer recommend?
options: Grant the roles directly to each user in each project by running a script.
Create a Google group, grant the four roles to it, and manage the membership in the group.
Grant the Owner role to the team lead and let them manage the other engineers.
Create one shared service account for all of the engineers to use.
questions.correct_rationale: Granting roles to groups means onboarding and offboarding only require group membership changes, and granting on a folder reduces bindings further.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-user bindings are hard to maintain, Owner is overly broad, and shared service accounts remove individual accountability.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A developer needs to create, start, stop, and delete Compute Engine VMs in a project but must not be able to modify networks, firewall rules, or IAM policies. Which role should the engineer grant?
options: `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`, the Compute Instance Admin role for VMs
`roles/editor`, the basic Editor role over all services
`roles/compute.admin`, the Compute Admin role with full control
`roles/compute.networkAdmin`, the Compute Network Admin role
questions.correct_rationale: Compute Instance Admin (v1) grants full control of instances without network or IAM administration permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Editor grants broad write access across services, Compute Admin includes networking and firewall control, and Network Admin is for networking rather than instances.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A security team needs a role that lets auditors list and get Compute Engine instances and Cloud Storage bucket metadata, but not read object contents. The same role must be reusable across 50 projects in the organization. What should the engineer do?
options: Grant the Viewer basic role in each of the projects for the auditors across the subscriptions.
Create a custom role in each folder that holds the projects.
Grant `roles/storage.objectViewer` and `roles/compute.viewer` to the auditors in every region.
Create an organization-level custom role with only the needed `list` and `get` permissions.
questions.correct_rationale: Custom roles can be created at the organization or project level, and an organization-level custom role can be granted on any project in the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Viewer is broader than necessary, custom roles can't be created at the folder level, and Storage Object Viewer grants access to object contents.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A company's security policy states that no VM may have an external IP address, except for two bastion VMs in a specific project. Engineers keep creating VMs with external IPs. What should the administrator implement?
options: Use a firewall rule that denies all ingress from the internet to the VMs.
Use an IAM deny policy on `compute.addresses.create` for the developers.
Use `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess` at the organization level, allowing only the two bastion VMs.
Use a Cloud Monitoring alert that fires when an external IP is assigned.
questions.correct_rationale: The `vmExternalIpAccess` list constraint defines which VM instances may have external IPs, preventing all others at creation time.
questions.distractor_summary: Firewall rules don't stop IP assignment, denying address creation doesn't block ephemeral external IPs, and alerts detect rather than prevent.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: An organization policy set at the organization level restricts VM creation to specific machine families. One research project needs an exception to use GPU machine types. How should the engineer allow this with minimal impact?
options: Set a policy on the research project that overrides the parent with the needed allowed values.
Remove the organization-level policy so that no project is restricted by it in the project as a result.
Move the research project out of the organization to avoid the policy.
Grant the team the Organization Policy Administrator role so they can ignore constraints at that point.
questions.correct_rationale: Organization policies can be set on a project to override or merge with inherited policies, creating a targeted exception.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing the org policy affects everyone, moving projects out of the organization loses governance, and a role grant doesn't bypass enforcement—it only lets someone change policies.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A European company must ensure that new resources such as Cloud Storage buckets, Compute Engine disks, and BigQuery datasets are created only in EU locations, across all current and future projects. What should the engineer configure?
options: Use `constraints/gcp.resourceLocations` at the organization with value group `in:eu-locations`.
Put `region=eu` labels on each project that hosts the resources.
Use VPC firewall rules that block the regions outside of the EU.
Use a budget alert on the spending outside of the EU regions.
questions.correct_rationale: The resource locations constraint restricts where location-based resources can be created, and value groups such as `in:eu-locations` cover EU regions and multi-regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Labels aren't enforced, firewall rules control traffic rather than resource placement, and budgets don't prevent creation.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A company discovered that a developer granted IAM roles on a production project to a personal Gmail account. Security wants to prevent anyone from granting IAM roles to identities outside the company's Cloud Identity domain. What should the engineer configure?
options: Remove the Gmail account and send a policy reminder to all of the developers.
Restrict API access with VPC Service Controls around the projects of the company.
Turn on Cloud Audit Logs to review the IAM changes that the developers make.
Set `constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` to the company's Cloud Identity customer ID.
questions.correct_rationale: Domain restricted sharing, implemented with `allowedPolicyMemberDomains`, prevents IAM bindings to principals outside the allowed customer IDs.
questions.distractor_summary: A reminder isn't enforcement, VPC Service Controls protects APIs rather than IAM membership, and audit logs only detect after the fact.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: Every new project automatically gets a `default` VPC with permissive firewall rules, which the security team must delete manually. The team wants new projects created without the default network. What should the engineer do?
options: Delete the default network via a startup script running on each VM.
Add an organization firewall rule that blocks the default network.
Enforce the `constraints/compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation` policy at the organization level.
Disable the Compute Engine API in every project of the organization.
questions.correct_rationale: The `skipDefaultNetworkCreation` boolean constraint prevents the default network from being created when the Compute Engine API is enabled in new projects.
questions.distractor_summary: VM startup scripts can't govern project networking, firewall rules don't stop network creation, and disabling Compute Engine prevents all VM usage.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A developer runs `gcloud pubsub topics create orders` in a new project and receives an error that the Pub/Sub API has not been used in the project before or is disabled. What should the developer do?
options: Enable the API with `gcloud services enable pubsub.googleapis.com`, then retry the command.
Request a Pub/Sub quota increase for the project and then retry it throughout the organization.
Link a new billing account to the project and then retry the command across the subscriptions.
Re-authenticate with `gcloud auth login` and then retry the command across the subscriptions.
questions.correct_rationale: Most Google Cloud APIs must be enabled per project before use, which `gcloud services enable` does.
questions.distractor_summary: The error is about enablement rather than quota or billing, and re-authenticating doesn't enable services.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A CI/CD service account provisions new environments and must be able to enable and disable Google Cloud APIs in projects it creates. Security wants to avoid granting Editor or Owner. Which role should the engineer grant?
options: `roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator`, the Project Creator role
`roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin`, the Service Usage Admin role
`roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`, the Service Account User role
`roles/browser`, the Browser role with read-only browsing access
questions.correct_rationale: Service Usage Admin includes the permissions to enable and disable services without broader editing rights.
questions.distractor_summary: Project Creator only creates projects, Service Account User allows acting as service accounts, and Browser grants read-only hierarchy access.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: An operations team supports 12 projects and wants to view dashboards and create alerts across all of them from a single place in Cloud Monitoring, without switching projects. What should the engineer configure?
options: Export each project's metrics to BigQuery and build the dashboards there.
Create a log sink in each project that sends the logs to a central bucket.
Grant Monitoring Viewer on each project and use the project picker for the views.
Make a scoping project and add the 12 projects to its metrics scope.
questions.correct_rationale: A metrics scope lets one scoping project view and alert on metrics from multiple monitored projects.
questions.distractor_summary: BigQuery exports add complexity and delay, log sinks handle logs rather than metrics, and switching projects doesn't give a unified view.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A company plans a product launch in three weeks that will require 800 vCPUs of N2 instances in `us-central1`. The current regional CPU quota is 500. What should the engineer do now?
options: Wait until the launch and request more quota if the instance creation fails in every region.
Split the workload across several projects without checking the quotas.
Request an N2 CPU quota increase for `us-central1` on the Quotas page, well before launch.
Upgrade the project's support plan, which removes the quotas of the project.
questions.correct_rationale: Quota increases are requested through the Quotas page and may take time to approve, so planning ahead avoids launch failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Waiting risks failed launches, other projects have their own quotas that also need checking, and support plans don't remove quotas.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: During an urgent incident, a team can't create additional VMs in `europe-west1` because it has reached its regional CPU quota, and the quota increase request is pending review. The application can run in any EU region. What is the fastest way to add capacity?
options: Create the VMs in another EU region, such as `europe-west4`, which has quota available.
Delete the project's quota limits in the console so that the VMs can be created in Azure.
Stop all of the VMs and start them again to free up the quota.
Change the VMs to a custom machine type, which does not count against the quota in Azure.
questions.correct_rationale: Regional quotas are separate per region, so deploying in another region with available quota adds capacity immediately.
questions.distractor_summary: Quotas can't be deleted by users, restarting VMs doesn't free quota, and custom machine types still count against CPU quota.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: An engineer works in a development project with a personal account and in a production project with a separate admin account, and frequently runs the wrong gcloud command against the wrong project. What should the engineer do?
options: Reinstall the Google Cloud CLI each time they switch between the two projects in every region.
Create a gcloud named configuration for each account and project and activate the right one.
Use Cloud Shell only for production and a browser for the development project in every region.
Set `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT` in a shared profile that is used for both of them in every region.
questions.correct_rationale: Named configurations store account, project, and default settings, making switching between environments explicit and fast.
questions.distractor_summary: Reinstalling is impractical, splitting tools doesn't prevent mistakes, and a single shared environment variable points both contexts at the same project.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A team created a project with the ID `acme-prj-test-01` and the name "Test Project." It now wants to rename it for production use. Which statement is correct?
options: Both the project ID and the name can be changed after the project is created.
Only the project number can be changed after the project is created.
The project ID can be changed, but the project name can't be changed.
The project name can be changed, but the project ID is permanent.
questions.correct_rationale: Project names are editable display labels, while project IDs are globally unique and immutable once created.
questions.distractor_summary: Project numbers are also assigned by Google and can't be changed.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A developer accidentally deleted a project containing important test data two days ago. What should the engineer do?
options: Contact support, because deleted projects can't be restored once they are deleted overall.
Create a new project that uses the same project ID as the deleted one.
Run `gcloud projects undelete`, since projects stay pending deletion for about 30 days.
Restore the project from the billing export that is kept for the account in every region.
questions.correct_rationale: Deleted projects are shut down and marked for deletion, and they can be restored during the roughly 30-day recovery period.
questions.distractor_summary: Project IDs can't be reused, support isn't required for restoration within the window, and billing exports don't contain resources.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A central networking project hosts a Shared VPC used by 60 service projects. Security wants to guarantee that nobody, including project Owners, can accidentally delete this project. What should the engineer configure?
options: Place a lien on the project that blocks its deletion until the lien is removed.
Remove all of the Owner role bindings on the project to protect it.
Create a daily project snapshot that can be used to restore it.
Set an organization policy that disables the project deletion globally as needed.
questions.correct_rationale: A lien prevents project deletion until it's removed, protecting critical projects from accidental deletion.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing Owners doesn't prevent other principals with delete permissions, projects can't be snapshotted, and a global restriction would block legitimate deletions in other projects.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: An administrator moved a project from the `Engineering` folder to the `Shared-Services` folder. Afterward, engineers who previously had access lost their permissions on the project, and a different organization policy now applies. What caused this?
options: Moving a project deletes its project-level IAM bindings throughout the organization for the team.
Roles and policies from the old folder stop applying; the project inherits from the new folder.
Moving a project resets all of the APIs that were enabled in it throughout the organization overall.
The project was moved to a different billing account when it moved throughout the organization overall.
questions.correct_rationale: Inherited policies come from the project's ancestors, so moving it changes which folder-level IAM bindings and organization policies apply, while project-level bindings remain.
questions.distractor_summary: Moving doesn't reset APIs or billing, and direct project bindings are preserved.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A user reports that they can't delete objects in a Cloud Storage bucket even though an administrator believes the user was granted the correct role at the folder level. The administrator wants to determine exactly why access is denied. What should the administrator use?
options: Use Cloud Monitoring dashboards to find out why the user cannot delete objects overall.
Use VPC Flow Logs to find out why the user cannot delete the objects.
Use IAM Recommender to find out why the user cannot delete the objects for the team.
Use Policy Troubleshooter with the user, the bucket and `storage.objects.delete`.
questions.correct_rationale: Policy Troubleshooter evaluates the relevant allow and deny policies to explain why a principal does or doesn't have a permission on a resource.
questions.distractor_summary: Monitoring and flow logs don't evaluate IAM, and IAM Recommender suggests removing excess permissions rather than diagnosing denials.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A security review found that many users hold the Editor role but appear to use only a few permissions. The team wants data-driven suggestions for replacing these grants with smaller roles. What should the engineer use?
options: Use Policy Troubleshooter to remove the unused permissions of the users.
Use organization policies to remove the unused permissions of the users.
Use IAM role recommendations from Recommender, based on the observed permission usage.
Use Security Command Center firewall findings to remove the unused permissions in Azure.
questions.correct_rationale: IAM role recommendations analyze permission usage over time and suggest removing or replacing roles with smaller ones.
questions.distractor_summary: Policy Troubleshooter explains specific access decisions, organization policies constrain resource configurations, and firewall findings concern network exposure.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: Security notices from Google about the organization's projects are being sent to a former employee's inbox. The company wants technical, security, and billing notifications to reach the appropriate team mailing lists at the organization level. What should the engineer configure?
options: Use Essential Contacts at the organization, with team emails for the notification categories.
Use a Cloud Monitoring notification channel for each of the teams in the organization across the setup.
Grant the Organization Administrator role to each of the team mailing lists.
Use billing budget alerts that are sent to each of the teams of the company.
questions.correct_rationale: Essential Contacts routes Google Cloud notifications by category, such as security, technical, and billing, and can be set at the organization, folder, or project level.
questions.distractor_summary: Monitoring channels are for alerts you define, IAM roles don't control notification routing, and budget alerts cover only spending.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Setting up cloud projects and accounts
questions.question: A company wants to attribute cost to teams in billing reports and also grant IAM roles conditionally so that a group can only administer resources marked as `environment=dev`. Which combination should the engineer use?
options: Use labels for both the cost reporting and the conditional IAM access throughout the organization overall.
Use labels for billing cost attribution, and Resource Manager tags with IAM Conditions for access.
Use network tags for both the cost reporting and the conditional IAM access across the subscriptions.
Use tags for the cost attribution and labels for the IAM Conditions throughout the organization overall.
questions.correct_rationale: Labels are key-value metadata that appear in billing exports and reports, while Resource Manager tags are IAM-controlled and can be referenced in IAM Conditions and organization policies.
questions.distractor_summary: Labels aren't intended for access control, and network tags are for firewall rules and routes.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A project owner tries to link a new project to the company's billing account and receives a permission error. The owner has the Owner role on the project. What additional role does the owner need?
options: Billing Account Viewer on the billing account, granted to the project owner.
Organization Viewer on the organization, granted to the project owner overall.
Project Billing Manager on the project, granted to the project owner.
Billing Account User on the billing account, granted to the project owner.
questions.correct_rationale: Linking a project to a billing account requires permission on both sides: Owner or Project Billing Manager on the project and Billing Account User (or Administrator) on the billing account.
questions.distractor_summary: The owner already has project-side permissions, and viewer roles don't allow linking.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: The finance team needs to view costs, invoices, and billing reports for the company's billing account, but must not be able to link projects, change payment settings, or manage billing permissions. Which role should the engineer grant?
options: Billing Account Administrator, which includes the rights to manage the account.
Billing Account User, which lets users link projects to the billing account.
Billing Account Viewer, which gives read-only access to costs and reports.
Project Billing Manager, which lets users link or unlink project billing.
questions.correct_rationale: Billing Account Viewer provides read access to billing information, including costs and transactions, without the ability to modify anything.
questions.distractor_summary: Administrator manages everything, Billing Account User can link projects, and Project Billing Manager manages project billing links.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A company set a $5,000 monthly budget with alerts at 50%, 90%, and 100% for a development project. Spending reached $7,200 this month despite the alerts. The manager asks why Google Cloud allowed spending past the budget. What should the engineer explain?
options: Budgets send notifications at the thresholds but do not cap spending or stop resources.
The budget was misconfigured, since budgets automatically disable billing at 100% for the team.
Budgets apply only to Compute Engine spending in the development project.
Budgets only take effect after they have been active for 90 days.
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Billing budgets trigger alerts but don't automatically stop usage, so exceeding the budget is possible unless automation is added.
questions.distractor_summary: Budgets can cover all services and take effect immediately, and they never disable billing on their own.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A university gives students sandbox projects with a strict $100 limit each. When a project reaches its budget, all its resources must stop automatically. What should the engineer implement?
options: Set a budget with an email alert to the professor at the 100% threshold across the subscriptions.
Publish the budget's notifications to Pub/Sub and use a Cloud Run function to disable billing.
Use the Compute Engine quota to limit the spending of each project throughout the organization overall.
Set labels on each project that hold the budget amount for each student across the subscriptions.
questions.correct_rationale: Programmatic budget notifications to Pub/Sub can trigger automation that unlinks billing, stopping billable resources, which is Google's documented approach to capping costs.
questions.distractor_summary: Email alerts require manual action, quotas limit resources rather than spend, and labels don't enforce limits.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A company wants early warning if the BigQuery spending in its analytics projects is likely to exceed $20,000 by month-end, even before actual spending gets close. What should the engineer configure?
options: Use a budget for the whole billing account with an actual-spend alert at 100% for the application.
Use a daily billing export query that the finance team runs manually.
Use a Cloud Monitoring alert on the BigQuery slot usage of the projects across the subscriptions.
Use a budget scoped to the analytics projects and BigQuery with a forecasted-spend threshold.
questions.correct_rationale: Budgets can be filtered by project, service, and labels, and threshold rules can be based on forecasted rather than actual spend, giving early warning.
questions.distractor_summary: A billing-account-wide budget lacks focus, manual queries aren't proactive, and slot usage doesn't directly represent dollars across pricing models.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: The finance team wants to analyze Google Cloud costs down to individual resources, such as specific VM instances and persistent disks, using SQL and custom dashboards in Looker Studio. What should the engineer set up?
options: Use the Cloud Billing reports in the console only, without any export.
Export the invoices as PDF files every month for the finance team.
Use Cloud Billing export to BigQuery with detailed usage cost data enabled.
Use a Cloud Monitoring dashboard with the CPU metrics of each resource overall.
questions.correct_rationale: The detailed usage cost export includes resource-level information in BigQuery, supporting SQL analysis and dashboards.
questions.distractor_summary: Console reports don't provide resource-level SQL analysis, PDF invoices aren't queryable, and CPU metrics aren't costs.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Multiple teams share a single project, and finance wants to see how much each team's resources cost. What should the engineer do?
options: Apply consistent labels such as `team=checkout` and group costs by them in billing.
Create a separate billing account for each team inside the same project for the team.
Use network tags on the VMs to separate the costs of the teams across the subscriptions.
Ask each team to estimate its own share of the costs by hand across the subscriptions.
questions.correct_rationale: Labels are included in billing data, so costs can be grouped and filtered by team in reports and BigQuery exports.
questions.distractor_summary: A project can only be linked to one billing account, network tags don't appear in billing, and manual estimates are inaccurate.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A manager wants a quick visual view of which Google Cloud services and SKUs drove last month's spending increase for a billing account, without setting up any data pipelines. What should the engineer use?
options: Use the billing export to BigQuery with a custom Looker dashboard for the manager.
Use Cloud Billing reports grouped by service and SKU, compared with last month.
Use Cloud Monitoring usage metrics to see which services drove the cost.
Use the Pricing Calculator to see which services drove the cost last month overall.
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Billing reports provide built-in charts with grouping and filtering by service, SKU, project, and time range, requiring no setup.
questions.distractor_summary: A BigQuery pipeline is more effort than needed, Monitoring doesn't show cost, and the Pricing Calculator estimates future costs.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A company bought Compute Engine committed use discounts in one project, but its steady-state workloads now run across 10 projects on the same billing account. The discount is underused. What should the engineer do?
options: Move all of the workloads into the single project that holds the commitments at that point.
Cancel the commitments and buy new ones in each of the projects.
Switch the workloads to Spot VMs instead of using the commitments in the project as a result.
Enable committed use discount sharing on the billing account so linked projects benefit.
questions.correct_rationale: Discount sharing lets commitments apply to eligible usage across projects on the same billing account.
questions.distractor_summary: Consolidating projects is disruptive, commitments generally can't be canceled, and Spot VMs aren't appropriate for steady-state workloads that need reliability.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A large enterprise's procurement department requires monthly invoices paid by bank transfer under net payment terms, rather than automatic credit card charges. What should the engineer recommend?
options: Keep a self-serve billing account and use several credit cards for the payments.
Create one billing account for each project and pay each by card.
Apply for an invoiced (offline) billing account through Google Cloud sales.
Use Google Workspace billing to pay the Google Cloud invoices by transfer.
questions.correct_rationale: Invoiced billing accounts are billed monthly and paid by invoice under agreed terms, subject to eligibility.
questions.distractor_summary: Self-serve accounts charge a payment instrument automatically, more billing accounts don't change payment method, and Workspace billing is separate.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Finance wants to stop charges for a project by disabling its billing. The project contains Compute Engine VMs, persistent disks, and Cloud Storage data that the team may need later. What should the engineer warn about?
options: Disabling billing stops paid services and can delete resources, so back up data first.
Disabling billing has no effect on the resources that are already running in production.
Disabling billing only pauses the VMs, while disks and storage are kept forever overall.
Billing can't be disabled for projects that are in an organization.
questions.correct_rationale: Without billing, paid resources are stopped and may eventually be deleted, so needed data should be protected first.
questions.distractor_summary: Running resources are affected, retention isn't guaranteed, and project billing can be disabled regardless of organization membership.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: A holding company operates three subsidiaries in one Google Cloud organization. Each subsidiary pays its own cloud costs and needs its own invoices. What should the engineer set up?
options: Use a single billing account with labels for each of the subsidiaries in every region.
Use a billing account for each subsidiary, with its projects linked to that account.
Use one billing account and a budget for each of the subsidiaries for the application.
Use separate organizations and one shared billing account for all of them for the team.
questions.correct_rationale: Each billing account produces its own invoices and payment relationship, so separate accounts match separate payers while keeping one organization for governance.
questions.distractor_summary: Labels and budgets don't split invoices, and splitting organizations fragments governance without separating payment.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Budget alerts for a project are only reaching billing administrators, but the project's engineering team needs to receive them in its team channel. What should the engineer configure?
options: Grant every engineer the Billing Account Administrator role for the project across the setup.
Create a log-based metric on the billing logs for the engineers.
Set up a billing export to BigQuery for the engineering team to query.
Link Monitoring notification channels, such as the team's email list, to the budget alerts.
questions.correct_rationale: By default, budget emails go to billing administrators and users, but budgets can also notify Cloud Monitoring notification channels chosen for the team.
questions.distractor_summary: Granting billing admin roles violates least privilege, and billing logs and exports don't send alerts.

questions.domain: 1. Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: An automation script must link a newly created project, `analytics-dev-042`, to billing account `012345-6789AB-CDEF01`. Which command should the script run?
options: `gcloud projects update analytics-dev-042 --billing-account=012345-6789AB-CDEF01`
`gcloud config set billing 012345-6789AB-CDEF01 --project=analytics-dev-042`
`gcloud billing projects link analytics-dev-042 --billing-account=012345-6789AB-CDEF01`
`gcloud services enable cloudbilling.googleapis.com --project=analytics-dev-042`
questions.correct_rationale: `gcloud billing projects link` associates a project with a billing account.
questions.distractor_summary: The other commands don't exist in that form, and enabling the Cloud Billing API doesn't link a project.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A startup has containerized a stateless REST API that receives unpredictable traffic, often with no requests overnight. The team has no operations staff, wants to pay nothing when idle, and needs HTTPS endpoints with automatic scaling. Which compute service should the engineer choose?
options: Compute Engine managed instance group with autoscaling and a minimum of one instance.
GKE Standard cluster with the cluster autoscaler enabled for the API.
Cloud Run, which scales the container automatically, including down to zero.
Compute Engine Spot VMs behind a load balancer for the REST API.
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Run runs stateless containers with managed HTTPS, automatic scaling, and scale to zero, so there's no cost when idle and no infrastructure to manage.
questions.distractor_summary: MIGs and GKE Standard require infrastructure management and keep at least some capacity running, and Spot VMs can be preempted and still need management.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A marketing team uploads images to a Cloud Storage bucket several times a day. Each upload must trigger a short piece of Python code that generates a thumbnail. The team wants minimal code and no servers to manage. What should the engineer use?
options: A Cloud Run function triggered by the Cloud Storage object finalize event.
A Compute Engine VM that polls the bucket every minute for new images overall.
A GKE CronJob that scans the bucket every hour for new images in production.
A Dataflow streaming pipeline that reads the new images from the bucket overall.
questions.correct_rationale: Event-driven functions triggered by Cloud Storage events run small pieces of code in response to uploads, with no servers to manage and no idle cost.
questions.distractor_summary: Polling VMs and CronJobs add management overhead and latency, and Dataflow is excessive for simple per-file processing.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company must migrate a legacy application that runs only on a specific older Linux distribution with a custom kernel module. The application can't be containerized and requires full control of the operating system. Which compute option should the engineer choose?
options: Cloud Run, which runs a container that holds the legacy application overall.
GKE Autopilot, which runs a container that holds the legacy application overall.
Cloud Run functions, which run the legacy application as a function.
Compute Engine, using a custom image that is built from the required OS.
questions.correct_rationale: Compute Engine gives full OS control, including custom images and kernel modules, which serverless and managed container platforms don't allow.
questions.distractor_summary: Cloud Run and Cloud Run functions run containers or code on managed runtimes, and Autopilot restricts node-level customization.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A platform team runs microservices on Kubernetes. It needs to install a node-level security agent as a DaemonSet with privileged access, tune kernel parameters on nodes, and choose specific GPU machine types for some node pools. Which option best fits these requirements?
options: GKE Autopilot, where the node configuration is managed by Google.
GKE Standard, where the team controls the nodes and can install node agents.
Cloud Run, where the nodes are fully managed by Google for the services.
Compute Engine MIGs without Kubernetes, which is not the platform they run overall.
questions.correct_rationale: GKE Standard gives full control over nodes and node pools, including privileged DaemonSets, node configuration, and machine types.
questions.distractor_summary: Autopilot restricts privileged workloads and node-level customization, Cloud Run isn't Kubernetes, and plain MIGs would require building orchestration from scratch.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A small team wants to run containerized applications on Kubernetes but doesn't want to manage nodes, upgrades, or capacity planning. It wants to pay based on the resources requested by its Pods and have Google apply security best practices by default. Which option should the engineer choose?
options: GKE Autopilot, where Google manages the nodes, scaling and node pools.
GKE Standard with node auto-provisioning, where the team manages the nodes.
A self-managed Kubernetes cluster on Compute Engine run by the team.
Compute Engine VMs with Container-Optimized OS that the team patches.
questions.correct_rationale: Autopilot manages nodes and infrastructure, bills for Pod resource requests, and enforces hardened defaults.
questions.distractor_summary: GKE Standard still involves node management and billing by node, and self-managed options increase operational work.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A research lab runs a nightly batch job that processes thousands of independent files. The job checkpoints progress, tolerates interruptions, and can run for longer than 24 hours when data volume is high. The lab wants the lowest compute cost. What should the engineer choose?
options: Use standard on-demand VMs with committed use discounts for the batch job overall.
Use Preemptible VMs, since they are cheapest and run for as long as needed.
Use Spot VMs, which offer deep discounts and can be preempted at any time.
Use sole-tenant nodes for the batch job to lower the cost of the VMs overall.
questions.correct_rationale: Spot VMs provide large discounts for fault-tolerant workloads and, unlike legacy preemptible VMs, don't have a 24-hour maximum runtime.
questions.distractor_summary: Committed use discounts suit steady workloads, preemptible VMs stop after 24 hours, and sole-tenant nodes cost more.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An application needs exactly 6 vCPUs and 40 GB of memory. The closest predefined N2 machine types either have too little memory or twice as many vCPUs as needed, increasing licensing costs. What should the engineer do?
options: Use `n2-highmem-8` to get enough memory, and accept the extra vCPUs.
Use `n2-standard-8` and add swap space to make up for the memory.
Use `e2-highmem-4` and accept fewer vCPUs than the application needs.
Create an N2 custom machine type with 6 vCPUs and 40 GB of memory.
questions.correct_rationale: Custom machine types let you choose vCPU and memory amounts within the family's limits, so 6 vCPUs and 40 GB fits N2 without paying for extra cores.
questions.distractor_summary: The predefined types either overprovision vCPUs or underprovision CPU or memory, and swap isn't a substitute for RAM.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company is deploying SAP HANA, which requires several terabytes of memory on a single VM. Which Compute Engine machine family should the engineer select?
options: E2 general-purpose machines, which offer a balanced cost for the workload overall.
M-series memory-optimized machines, which offer terabytes of memory in one VM.
C3 compute-optimized machines, which offer the highest CPU performance.
A2 accelerator-optimized machines, which attach GPUs to the workload.
questions.correct_rationale: Memory-optimized M-series machines provide the very large memory footprints required by in-memory databases like SAP HANA. E2 has limited memory, compute-optimized families favor CPU performance, and accelerator-optimized families are built for GPUs.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A team has a containerized data-export task that runs once per night, processes records for 20 minutes, and then exits. It doesn't serve HTTP requests. The team wants a serverless option with no cluster to manage. What should the engineer use?
options: Use Cloud Run jobs triggered on a schedule by Cloud Scheduler.
Use a Cloud Run service with a minimum of one instance kept running.
Use a GKE Standard cluster with a CronJob that runs the task overall.
Use an always-on Compute Engine VM with cron that runs the task.
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Run jobs run containers to completion without needing to serve requests, and they can be scheduled with Cloud Scheduler.
questions.distractor_summary: Cloud Run services are designed for request handling, and GKE or VMs add infrastructure to manage and pay for when idle.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A data science team needs VMs with NVIDIA GPUs to train deep learning models in `us-central1`. What should the engineer check before planning the deployment?
options: Check that Private Google Access is enabled in the region for the VMs throughout the organization.
Check that the project uses Standard Tier networking for the GPU VMs.
Check that the GPU types and machine types exist in the zones, and that GPU quota is available.
Check that the VMs use preemptible instances, which are required for the GPUs for the application.
questions.correct_rationale: GPU models and machine types vary by zone, and GPU quota is separate and often starts low, so both must be verified.
questions.distractor_summary: Private Google Access and network tier don't affect GPU availability, and GPUs work with on-demand VMs as well as Spot or preemptible VMs.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A healthcare company processes sensitive patient data on Compute Engine. A new requirement mandates that data be encrypted while in use in memory, not only at rest and in transit, with minimal application changes. What should the engineer choose?
options: Shielded VMs with Secure Boot, which protect the boot integrity of the VMs.
Customer-managed encryption keys, which encrypt the persistent disks of the VMs.
Sole-tenant nodes, which isolate the VMs on hardware that the company alone uses.
Confidential VMs, which encrypt the data while it is in use in memory.
questions.correct_rationale: Confidential VMs use hardware-based memory encryption to protect data in use without requiring application changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Shielded VMs protect boot integrity, CMEK protects data at rest, and sole-tenant nodes provide physical isolation rather than memory encryption.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company is moving Windows Server and SQL Server workloads to Compute Engine and wants to reuse its existing per-core licenses. The licensing terms require dedicated physical servers that aren't shared with other customers. What should the engineer use?
options: Spot VMs, which lower the cost of the licensed workloads on Compute Engine overall.
Sole-tenant nodes, which give dedicated hardware for bring-your-own licenses.
Confidential VMs, which encrypt the memory of the licensed workloads.
Cloud Run with Windows containers, which hosts the licensed workloads in Azure.
questions.correct_rationale: Sole-tenant nodes provide physical servers dedicated to one project, supporting bring-your-own-license scenarios that require dedicated hardware.
questions.distractor_summary: Spot and Confidential VMs still run on shared hosts, and Cloud Run doesn't support Windows containers.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A global gaming company needs a relational database for player accounts and in-game purchases. It must support strongly consistent transactions across users in North America, Europe, and Asia, scale horizontally beyond a single machine, and offer up to 99.999% availability. Which database should the engineer choose?
options: Use Spanner with a multi-region configuration for the accounts.
Use Cloud SQL for MySQL with cross-region read replicas for the accounts.
Use Bigtable with multi-cluster replication for the accounts.
Use Firestore in Datastore mode for the accounts.
questions.correct_rationale: Spanner provides globally distributed, strongly consistent relational transactions with horizontal scaling and a 99.999% multi-region SLA. Cloud SQL scales vertically and its read replicas are asynchronous, Bigtable isn't relational, and Firestore isn't a relational SQL database.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An energy company collects readings from 2 million sensors every second. It needs to store petabytes of time-series data and serve single-digit-millisecond reads by sensor ID and time range. SQL joins aren't required. Which service should the engineer choose?
options: Use Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL to store the sensor readings as needed.
Use BigQuery to store the sensor readings as they arrive by default.
Use Bigtable, a wide-column store built for high write throughput.
Use Firestore to store the sensor readings as documents for the team.
questions.correct_rationale: Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL database designed for very high write throughput and low-latency key and range lookups at petabyte scale, which fits time-series data.
questions.distractor_summary: Cloud SQL doesn't scale to this write volume, BigQuery is optimized for analytics rather than low-latency serving, and Firestore isn't designed for this throughput.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company is building a mobile and web app where users edit shared to-do lists. It needs a serverless document database with real-time updates to connected clients, offline support on devices, and automatic scaling. Which service should the engineer choose?
options: Use Cloud SQL to store the shared lists and sync them to clients.
Use Firestore in Native mode, which has real-time listeners and offline support.
Use Bigtable to store the shared lists and sync them to the clients in production.
Use Memorystore for Redis to store the shared lists for the clients in production.
questions.correct_rationale: Firestore in Native mode is a serverless document database with real-time listeners and offline support in its mobile and web SDKs.
questions.distractor_summary: Cloud SQL and Bigtable lack these client features, and Memorystore is an in-memory cache rather than a durable app database.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A retailer wants to analyze five years of sales data (about 300 TB) with standard SQL, run ad hoc queries by analysts, and connect Looker Studio dashboards, without managing infrastructure. Which service should the engineer choose?
options: Use Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL to run the SQL queries over the sales data.
Use Spanner to run the SQL queries over the 300 TB of sales data.
Use Bigtable to run the SQL queries over the 300 TB of sales data.
Use BigQuery, a serverless data warehouse for standard SQL analytics.
questions.correct_rationale: BigQuery is a serverless data warehouse for SQL analytics on large datasets and integrates with BI tools like Looker Studio.
questions.distractor_summary: Cloud SQL isn't built for analytics at this scale, Spanner targets transactional workloads, and Bigtable doesn't support standard SQL analytics well.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company is migrating a regional web application that uses a 500 GB MySQL database. It wants a managed service with automated backups, patching, and high availability, without changing the application. Which service should the engineer choose?
options: Use Cloud SQL for MySQL, a managed service with the same engine.
Use Spanner, which needs the schema and queries to be reworked first.
Run MySQL yourself on Compute Engine, with the patching and backups handled by the team.
Use Firestore, which needs the relational data to be reworked into documents.
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud SQL for MySQL is a managed MySQL service with backups, maintenance, and HA configuration, requiring no application change.
questions.distractor_summary: Spanner uses a different dialect and is designed for larger global scale, self-managed MySQL adds operational work, and Firestore isn't MySQL-compatible.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A financial analytics company runs a demanding PostgreSQL workload that mixes high-volume transactions with real-time analytical queries. It needs PostgreSQL compatibility, higher performance than standard managed PostgreSQL, and a fully managed service. Which service should the engineer recommend?
options: Use Cloud SQL for MySQL, which is a different engine from PostgreSQL for the application.
Use BigQuery, which is a warehouse and not a transactional database across the subscriptions.
Use AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, built for demanding mixed transactional and analytic loads.
Use Firestore, which is a document database and not a relational one for the application.
questions.correct_rationale: AlloyDB is a fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible database built for high transactional performance and fast analytical queries on the same data.
questions.distractor_summary: MySQL isn't PostgreSQL-compatible, BigQuery isn't a transactional database, and Firestore isn't relational.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A media company stores millions of objects in one bucket with unpredictable access patterns: some old files suddenly become popular, while many new files are never read. The team doesn't want to write or maintain lifecycle rules. What should the engineer configure?
options: Set the bucket to Autoclass so objects move between classes automatically as access changes.
Store everything in the Archive class to get the lowest storage cost across the subscriptions.
Create lifecycle rules that move objects to Coldline after 30 days.
Use a dual-region bucket so that the objects are kept in two regions across the subscriptions.
questions.correct_rationale: Autoclass automatically transitions objects to colder classes when not accessed and back to Standard when accessed, which fits unpredictable patterns without manual rules.
questions.distractor_summary: Archive would be expensive for frequently accessed files, fixed lifecycle rules don't respond to access, and location type doesn't affect storage class.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company needs a Cloud Storage bucket that stays available if an entire region becomes unavailable, with data stored in two specific US regions for compliance, and with a recovery point objective of 15 minutes for replication. What should the engineer configure?
options: Use a single-region bucket with object versioning enabled on the bucket as a result.
Use a multi-region `US` bucket, with its location spread over the country in the project.
Use a dual-region bucket in the needed regions with turbo replication enabled.
Use two single-region buckets with a daily Storage Transfer Service job.
questions.correct_rationale: Dual-region buckets let you choose the regions, and turbo replication provides a 15-minute RPO for replication between them.
questions.distractor_summary: A single region doesn't survive regional outages, a multi-region bucket doesn't let you choose specific regions or offer turbo replication, and daily transfers give a one-day RPO.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A self-managed PostgreSQL database on Compute Engine needs consistently high IOPS and low latency for its data volume, and the data must persist if the VM is stopped or recreated. Which disk option should the engineer choose?
options: Use Local SSD, which is fast but does not keep its data when the VM stops overall.
Use an SSD persistent disk (`pd-ssd`), which gives high IOPS and keeps its data.
Use a standard persistent disk (`pd-standard`), which is meant for sequential access.
Use a Cloud Storage bucket mounted with Cloud Storage FUSE for the database overall.
questions.correct_rationale: SSD persistent disks provide high IOPS with low latency and persist independently of the VM's lifecycle.
questions.distractor_summary: Local SSDs are faster but data doesn't persist when the VM stops, standard disks have lower performance, and Cloud Storage FUSE isn't suitable for database storage.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company runs a stateful application on a single Compute Engine VM in `us-east1-b`. It needs to recover quickly in another zone if `us-east1-b` fails, without losing any data written to disk. What should the engineer use?
options: Use a daily snapshot schedule of the zonal persistent disk of the VM for the team at that point in the project.
Use a local SSD with RAID 1 for the data of the application on the VM in the zone across the setup in that case.
Use a zonal persistent disk together with a machine image of the VM as a result across the setup in that case.
Use a regional persistent disk, replicated across two zones, attached to a standby VM on failover.
questions.correct_rationale: Regional persistent disks replicate writes synchronously between two zones, so the disk can be force-attached to a VM in the other zone with no data loss.
questions.distractor_summary: Snapshots and machine images lose data written since the last capture, and local SSDs are tied to one VM.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A video rendering job needs very high-throughput, low-latency scratch space for temporary files during processing. The files can be regenerated if lost, and the final output is written to Cloud Storage. What should the engineer attach to the VMs?
options: Use Local SSD, which gives very high throughput and low latency scratch space.
Use a regional persistent disk, which replicates the scratch data across zones.
Use Filestore, which provides a shared file system over the network.
Use a balanced persistent disk, which gives moderate performance at a lower cost.
questions.correct_rationale: Local SSDs are physically attached to the host for very high performance and are ideal for scratch data that can be lost.
questions.distractor_summary: Regional and balanced persistent disks cost more for lower performance on scratch data, and Filestore is shared network storage.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company is migrating a content management system in which 12 web servers need to read and write the same set of files concurrently through a POSIX-compliant NFS share. Which storage service should the engineer choose?
options: Attach one persistent disk to all 12 VMs in read-write mode.
Use Cloud Storage buckets accessed through the JSON API from each of the servers.
Use Filestore, a managed NFS file share that all of the web servers can mount.
Use Local SSDs on each of the VMs and copy the files between them.
questions.correct_rationale: Filestore provides managed NFS file shares that many VMs can mount concurrently for read and write.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard persistent disks can't be shared read-write across many VMs, Cloud Storage isn't an NFS file system, and local SSDs aren't shared.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An e-commerce site's Cloud SQL database is overloaded by repeated reads of the same product catalog data. The team wants to add a managed, in-memory cache with sub-millisecond latency in front of the database. What should the engineer use?
options: Use Bigtable as a cache in front of the Cloud SQL database.
Use Memorystore for Redis as an in-memory cache in front of the database.
Use Firestore as a cache in front of the Cloud SQL database in every region.
Use Cloud CDN to cache the database queries in front of Cloud SQL in Azure.
questions.correct_rationale: Memorystore for Redis is a managed in-memory data store commonly used as an application cache in front of databases.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigtable and Firestore are persistent databases, and Cloud CDN caches HTTP content at the edge rather than database query results.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company is creating its first production VPC. It needs subnets only in `us-central1` and `europe-west1` with IP ranges that don't overlap its on-premises networks (`10.0.0.0/9`). What should the engineer create?
options: Use an auto mode VPC, which creates subnets in every region automatically for the application.
Use the default network and then delete the subnets that are not needed for the application.
Use two separate VPCs, one for each of the two required regions throughout the organization.
Use a custom mode VPC with subnets in the two regions, with ranges outside `10.0.0.0/9`.
questions.correct_rationale: Custom mode VPCs let you choose regions and IP ranges, avoiding overlap with on-premises networks.
questions.distractor_summary: Auto mode and default networks create subnets in every region from `10.128.0.0/9`, and separate VPCs per region add unnecessary complexity because one VPC spans regions.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company serves a public HTTPS website to users worldwide from backends in three regions. It wants one global IP address, SSL termination, content-based routing, and automatic routing to the closest healthy backend. Which load balancer should the engineer choose?
options: Use a global external Application Load Balancer for the website.
Use an external passthrough Network Load Balancer for the website.
Use an internal Application Load Balancer for the website.
Use a regional external proxy Network Load Balancer for the website.
questions.correct_rationale: The global external Application Load Balancer provides a single anycast IP, HTTPS termination, URL-based routing, and cross-region failover.
questions.distractor_summary: Passthrough and proxy Network Load Balancers don't do content-based HTTP routing, and internal load balancers aren't internet-facing.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A three-tier application has application servers that connect to a pool of database proxy VMs on TCP 6432 in the same region. The traffic must remain private within the VPC, and the database proxies should see the application servers' IP addresses. Which load balancer should the engineer choose?
options: Use a global external Application Load Balancer for the database pool overall.
Use an internal Application Load Balancer for the database pool.
Use an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer for the database pool.
Use an external proxy Network Load Balancer for the database pool overall.
questions.correct_rationale: The internal passthrough Network Load Balancer distributes TCP traffic privately within a region while preserving client source IPs.
questions.distractor_summary: Application Load Balancers are for HTTP(S), and external load balancers are internet-facing.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company hosts a public download site for customers located mostly in the same country as its Google Cloud region. It wants to lower network egress costs and accepts somewhat lower network performance. What should the engineer configure?
options: Use Premium Tier with Cloud CDN for the external addresses.
Use Standard Tier for the external IP addresses, since users are in one region.
Use a global external Application Load Balancer in front of the site for the team.
Use Cloud Interconnect to connect the customers to the download site.
questions.correct_rationale: Standard Tier has lower egress pricing and routes traffic over the public internet closer to the region, which suits cost-sensitive regional audiences.
questions.distractor_summary: Premium Tier and global load balancing cost more, and Interconnect is for private connectivity to your own network.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company plans to deploy an application using a specific machine family and a specific GPU in `asia-southeast1`. Before finalizing the architecture, what should the engineer confirm?
options: Check that the region supports VPC Network Peering for the application for the team.
Check that the Cloud DNS API is enabled in the project for the application in Azure.
Check that the region has a proxy-only subnet for the application across the subscriptions.
Check that the machine family and the GPU are offered in the zones of that region.
questions.correct_rationale: Machine families, GPUs, and some services aren't available in every region or zone, so resource location availability must be checked during planning.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering, Cloud DNS, and proxy-only subnets aren't related to whether specific hardware is offered.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An engineer creates a subnet `app-subnet` in `us-central1`. The team wants to place VMs in zones `us-central1-a` and `us-central1-c` for resilience. What is true about the subnet?
options: Subnets are regional, so VMs in any zone of `us-central1` can use `app-subnet`.
Subnets are zonal, so a second subnet is needed for `us-central1-c` for the team.
Subnets are global, so VMs in any region can use `app-subnet` for the application.
Subnets must be created for each project and for each zone.
questions.correct_rationale: VPC networks are global, but subnets are regional resources available to all zones in their region.
questions.distractor_summary: They aren't zonal or global, and one subnet serves VMs across all zones of its region.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A small company needs encrypted connectivity between its office network and a Google Cloud VPC for a few hundred Mbps of traffic. It needs to be operational this week and can't justify colocation costs. What should the engineer recommend?
options: Use Dedicated Interconnect, which is a private link and not encrypted by default.
Use Partner Interconnect with a 10 Gbps attachment, which is more than needed.
Use HA VPN, which gives encrypted connectivity over the internet at a low cost.
Use Direct Peering, which connects to Google's network but not to a VPC.
questions.correct_rationale: HA VPN provides encrypted IPsec connectivity over the internet, can be set up quickly, and fits modest bandwidth needs.
questions.distractor_summary: Interconnect options take longer to provision and cost more, and Direct Peering doesn't provide private VPC access.

questions.domain: 2. Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company deploys VMs without external IP addresses for security. These VMs must upload backups to Cloud Storage. The company doesn't want to allow general internet access. What should the engineer configure?
options: Assign ephemeral external IPs to the VMs so they can reach Cloud Storage.
Enable Private Google Access on the subnet of the VMs for Cloud Storage.
Configure Cloud NAT for all of the traffic of the VMs.
Create a VPC Network Peering connection from the VPC to Cloud Storage.
questions.correct_rationale: Private Google Access lets VMs with only internal IPs reach Google APIs such as Cloud Storage without internet access.
questions.distractor_summary: External IPs expose the VMs, Cloud NAT allows general internet egress, and Cloud Storage isn't reachable through VPC Network Peering.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An engineer must create a VM named `api-01` in `us-central1-a` using an `e2-standard-4` machine type and the latest Debian 12 image. Security policy requires that the VM have no external IP address. Which command should the engineer run?
options: `gcloud compute instances create api-01 --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-standard-4 --image=debian-12 --no-address`
`gcloud compute instances create api-01 --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-standard-4 --image-family=debian-12 --image-project=debian-cloud --no-address`
`gcloud compute instances create api-01 --region=us-central1 --machine-type=e2-standard-4 --image-family=debian-12 --image-project=debian-cloud --no-address` overall.
`gcloud compute instances create api-01 --zone=us-central1-a --image-family=debian-12 --image-project=debian-cloud --network-tier=STANDARD --no-address` overall.
questions.correct_rationale: Using `--image-family` with `--image-project` selects the latest image in the family, and `--no-address` prevents an external IP. Option A references an image name that doesn't exist and assigns an external IP by default, VMs are zonal so `--region` isn't valid, and changing the network tier still assigns an external IP.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A web application runs on identical Compute Engine VMs. The team wants the VMs spread across multiple zones in `europe-west1`, with the number of instances automatically adjusted to keep average CPU utilization around 60%. What should the engineer create?
options: Use several standalone VMs in different zones, configured with a startup script overall.
Use an unmanaged instance group that has instances spread over multiple zones.
Use a zonal managed instance group with manual scaling of the instance count.
Use an instance template and a regional MIG with an autoscaling policy at 60% CPU.
questions.correct_rationale: A regional MIG distributes identical VMs from an instance template across zones and supports autoscaling on CPU utilization.
questions.distractor_summary: Standalone VMs and unmanaged groups don't autoscale, and a zonal MIG doesn't spread across zones.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A managed instance group with autohealing keeps deleting and recreating new VMs in a loop. Logs show that the application takes about four minutes to start, and the autohealing health check marks VMs unhealthy after about one minute. What should the engineer change?
options: Raise the autohealing initial delay above the application's startup time, such as five minutes.
Disable the health check entirely so that the group stops recreating VMs across the subscriptions.
Switch the group to a larger machine type so the application starts faster across the subscriptions.
Change the group to use Spot VMs so that the VMs are recreated less often across the subscriptions.
questions.correct_rationale: The initial delay gives new VMs time to start before autohealing health checks can trigger recreation.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling health checks removes autohealing, a larger VM may not shorten startup enough, and Spot VMs don't affect health checking.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An engineer is creating VMs with attached NVIDIA GPUs for a training workload and wants them to restart automatically after Google Cloud host maintenance events. The default availability policy settings cause VM creation to fail. What should the engineer set?
options: `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` and `--restart-on-failure` on the VMs overall.
`--preemptible` and `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` on the VMs.
`--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` and `--restart-on-failure` on the VMs.
`--no-restart-on-failure` only, with no other maintenance setting overall.
questions.correct_rationale: VMs with attached GPUs generally can't live-migrate, so the host maintenance policy must be `TERMINATE`, while automatic restart brings them back after maintenance. `MIGRATE` fails for these GPU VMs, preemptible VMs don't restart automatically, and disabling restart contradicts the requirement.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A security audit found that SSH keys added to project-wide metadata years ago still grant access to every VM in a project. The team wants a sensitive VM to accept only its own instance-level keys immediately, while it plans a wider move to OS Login. What should the engineer do for that VM?
options: Delete the boot disk of the VM and recreate it to remove the old keys overall.
Set the instance metadata key `block-project-ssh-keys` to `TRUE` on the VM.
Remove the Compute Engine default service account from the VM.
Create a firewall rule that denies TCP 22 from all of the sources.
questions.correct_rationale: The `block-project-ssh-keys` metadata setting prevents project-wide SSH keys from being used on that instance while keeping instance-level keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating disks is disruptive, service accounts don't control SSH keys, and denying TCP 22 blocks all SSH access.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: A company wants SSH access to Linux VMs to be controlled entirely through IAM, with access removed automatically when an employee leaves Cloud Identity. Administrators need sudo, developers don't, and all users must use two-step verification. What should the engineer configure?
options: Use project metadata SSH keys for each user, plus a shared sudo password.
Distribute service account keys to each user for their SSH logins.
Use IAP TCP forwarding only, with no OS Login enabled on the VMs.
Use OS Login with 2-step verification; `osAdminLogin` for admins, `osLogin` for developers.
questions.correct_rationale: OS Login ties Linux accounts to IAM and Cloud Identity, supports 2-step verification, and distinguishes sudo access with OS Admin Login.
questions.distractor_summary: Metadata keys and shared passwords aren't tied to identity lifecycle, service account keys aren't for humans, and IAP controls the network path rather than Linux account permissions.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An engineer adds a startup script to a VM's metadata to install and start Nginx, but after booting, Nginx isn't running. SSH access is restricted. How should the engineer troubleshoot?
options: View the serial port output, or the Cloud Logging logs, for the startup script's output.
Recreate the VM with a larger boot disk, then run the script again across the subscriptions.
Check the VPC Flow Logs of the VM for the failure of the script throughout the organization.
Enable Private Google Access on the subnet of the VM and retry throughout the organization.
questions.correct_rationale: Startup script output is written to the serial console and Cloud Logging, which reveal errors without SSH access.
questions.distractor_summary: Disk size, flow logs, and Private Google Access aren't likely causes of a failing startup script, though a script that downloads packages may need egress, which the logs would reveal.

questions.domain: 3. Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
